title: church words nobody defined
hookLine: quiet time, on fire, testimony: the church words you picked up like a family's inside jokes

cards: Quiet time. On fire for God. A hedge of protection.
Traveling mercies. If you grew up in church, you probably learned these the way you learn a family's inside jokes: by hearing them a lot. People even have a name for it: Christianese.
Today, three of them, and what's actually behind them.

teach.h: QUIET TIME — A HABIT OF JESUS.
teach.b: Quiet time means a few minutes alone each day to read the Bible and pray. It has a model. One Gospel says Jesus got up "a great while before day" and went off to a solitary place to pray.
On fire means eager, all in. It echoes two friends on a road who said, after a stranger turned out to be Jesus, that their hearts had burned inside them while he talked.
And testimony. At camp or youth group, someone stands by the bonfire and tells how they came to faith. Testimony is a courtroom word.

In Greek it's martyria, from martys: a witness, someone who says what they saw. Early Christians who died rather than take back what they'd witnessed were called by that same word, and it came into English as martyr.
So a testimony isn't a performance, and it isn't a sales pitch. It's a witness statement: here's what happened to me. Some people love telling theirs to a crowd.
Plenty of Christians keep theirs for a friend, or for nobody but God.

how: Many evangelical churches, youth groups and camps invite people to share a testimony, the story of how they came to faith, aloud; many Christians also keep a daily quiet time of Bible reading and prayer, often in the morning.

games.q: church words, decoded — tap the pairs.
p: time alone to read and pray
hearts that burned on a road

s: the word martyr first meant witness
Greek martys, a witness. it came to mean someone who died for what they witnessed.
quiet time is a phrase from the Bible
it's a church phrase, modeled on Jesus going off early to a solitary place to pray.
a testimony has to be dramatic
it's a witness statement: what happened to you. a quiet one counts.

games.q: after a long day of crowds, one Gospel shows Jesus the next morning. what does he do?
o: gets up a great while before day and goes off alone to pray.
starts teaching the crowd right away.
games.why: a great while before day, he went off to a solitary place to pray. that's the model behind a quiet time.

games.q: put the word's journey in order.
p: martyr: one who died for it

practice: Three breaths with the bell. On the first, think of one thing that really happened to you, something that changed you even a little. On the second, say to yourself, in one plain sentence, what happened.
On the third, let it rest. A witness doesn't add anything.

wordCard.voice: Testimony. From the Greek for witness: here's what I saw happen. Fifth word.

orig.note: Greek: testimony, witness. from martys, a witness, the root of English martyr.

carryVoice: Your line: your story is a witness. A quiet one counts as much as a bonfire one. Five days in.
